headline: WSJ reports Saudi courting Egypt military help, recruiting foreign fighters, concedes limits
dek: WSJ reports: (1) Egypt (Sisi spokesman) says prepared to provide military help to Saudi Arabia; (2) Saudi official: kingdom 'will take all necessary measures... Ansar Allah represent a global threat and require a global response'; (3) Saudi Arabia looking to recruit foreign fighters to help Yemeni…
sources: Wall Street Journal ('Saudi Arabia's Military Limitations Are Being Exposed by Ansar Allah Attacks')
fault_line: Is Egypt about to join a direct war with Yemen — and is Saudi Arabia admitting its own military can't handle the Ansar Allah?

sections.what_happened: WSJ reports: (1) Egypt (Sisi spokesman) says prepared to provide military help to Saudi Arabia; (2) Saudi official: kingdom 'will take all necessary measures... Ansar Allah represent a global threat and require a global response'; (3) Saudi Arabia looking to recruit foreign fighters to help Yemeni allies while open to diplomatic solution; (4) analysts (CSIS Allison Minor, ex-US deputy envoy for Yemen): Ansar Allah built mobile launchers and buried missile-production facilities and can absorb coalition airstrikes while hitting deep targets. Egypt pledge corroborated by CGTN, ToI, Berita Harian (emergency parliamentary session to approve deployment).
sections.what_verified: Egypt military-support pledge: CGTN, Times of Israel, France24 via Threads; Al Jazeera Egypt parliament item (vote postponed per 0700 scan, emergency session now sought). 'Foreign fighters recruitment' claim is WSJ single-source (people familiar with Saudi strategy) — attributed, not independently confirmed.
sections.what_disputed: None on the pledge itself; debate in Egyptian parliament delayed/deferred earlier (vote postponed), so deployment is pledged, not yet authorized.
sections.why_matters: Saudi asks Egypt to fight its war: WSJ concedes the kingdom is exposed — the Ansar Allah war is now a coalition test. Frame from the Gulf-street perspective, not Washington's: what does Cairo's army gain, and what does the Ansar Allah missile-production network imply for the next strike wave?
sections.context: Background: Saudi/Ansar Allah war — NEW: WSJ reports Saudi courting Egypt military help, recruiting foreign fighters, concedes limits; Egypt pledge confirmed

totw_analysis: Our read: Saudi asks Egypt to fight its war: WSJ concedes the kingdom is exposed — the Ansar Allah war is now a coalition test. Frame from the Gulf-street perspective, not Washington's: what does Cairo's army gain, and what does the Ansar Allah missile-production network imply for the next strike wave? The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Egypt about to join a direct war with Yemen — and is Saudi Arabia admitting its own military can't handle the Ansar Allah?
